finding.title: Stop TrackLearningOrderRepositoryImpl importing ContentRepository directly — compose in a service/notifier (SM-8)
finding.why: TrackLearningOrderRepositoryImpl takes a ContentRepository constructor dependency and calls `_contentRepository.getContentForCurriculum(...)` directly from three of its own methods (_buildSedarimIndex, _buildMasechtosIndex). This is exactly the repository-imports-repository shape SM-8 forbids: unit-testing this repository now requires faking or booting ContentRepository's dependency chain instead of a clean seam, and the file's own doc comments on MasechtaOrderingPolicy already flag this as a known-wrong coupling ('Unblocks W4.22 (_buildMasechtosIndex removal from the repository impl)') that the team is mid-way through unwinding.
finding.recommendation: Move the content-fetch + index-build orchestration into a domain service or the notifier that currently constructs TrackLearningOrderRepositoryImpl, passing the already-resolved content list/indices into the repository (or into MasechtaOrderingPolicy directly), so the repository itself only talks to its own DAO.
acceptance_criteria: TrackLearningOrderRepositoryImpl no longer imports anything under features/content_browsing/.
A unit test constructs TrackLearningOrderRepositoryImpl with only a fake/in-memory database (no ContentRepository fake required).
SM-8's grep/lint (once implemented) reports zero repository→repository imports in lib/features/tracks/.

finding.title: Wrap TrackLearningOrderRepositoryImpl's save/reset methods' two DAO writes in a single transaction (DB-2)
finding.why: saveSedarimOrder, saveMasechtosOrder, and resetToDefault each perform two sequential, separately-awaited local Drift writes (upsertOrder/deleteByTrack, then trackDao.stampReorderAt) with no shared transaction() wrapper. If the process dies between the two statements (app kill, OS low-memory kill — routine on mobile), the reorder is saved but the 'reorder-amnesty' stamp is not, so the scheduler keeps showing items as overdue that the user just reordered past — the exact bug the stampReorderAt call exists to prevent (per the file's own '§10.1' comments). stage_definition_repository_impl.dart's reorderStages in the same batch already demonstrates the correct pattern (_stageDao.runTransaction(...)) for the identical class of problem.
finding.recommendation: Wrap each pair of DAO calls in `_database.transaction(() async { ... })`, mirroring the pattern already used in stage_definition_repository_impl.dart.reorderStages.
acceptance_criteria: All three methods wrap both DAO calls in one _database.transaction() block.
A test that throws inside a mocked stampReorderAt asserts upsertOrder/deleteByTrack's effects are rolled back (not left partially applied).
DB-2's checker (once implemented) reports zero multi-statement-without-transaction sites in this file.

finding.title: Stop hardcoding TextDirection.rtl on TrackLabelStep's free-text field regardless of app locale
finding.why: TrackLabelStep's TextFormField is the free-text 'name this track' input — the user can type anything, in either app locale. Forcing textDirection: TextDirection.rtl unconditionally (not gated on locale or on the defaultLabel's script) means an English-locale user typing 'Morning Bavli Study' gets a right-anchored cursor/hint and base-RTL layout for a field the rest of the (LTR) English screen doesn't otherwise use RTL for. This is precisely what the currently-broken `no_hardcoded_text_direction` custom lint rule exists to catch — with custom_lint crashing repo-wide, nothing currently flags it.
finding.recommendation: Drive textDirection from the ambient Directionality/locale (or drop the explicit override and let Flutter's default locale-derived directionality apply), the same way other bidi-sensitive widgets in this batch (scope_views.dart's chooseLevelPrompt) key off useHebrew instead of hardcoding a direction.
acceptance_criteria: textDirection on this field is either removed or computed from Directionality.of(context)/a Hebrew-Terms-aware flag, not a literal TextDirection.rtl.
An EN-locale widget test asserts the field's effective text direction is ltr.
custom_lint's no_hardcoded_text_direction rule (once unbroken) passes on this file.

finding.title: Fix AX-1's EdgeInsets.only(left:/right:) grep to match multi-line dart-format output, and fix the resulting hit in track_management_body.dart
finding.why: track_management_body.dart:102-107 uses EdgeInsets.only(left: 16, right: 16, top: 8, bottom: 96) — the exact pattern AX-1 bans. The root Makefile's check 10/12 grep is single-line only (`[^)]*` cannot span the newline dart format inserts after 4+ named args), so `grep -rn 'EdgeInsets\.only([^)]*\(left\|right\):' lib/` returns zero hits repo-wide even though this exact violation exists; a `-Pzo` multiline reproduction confirms the hit. Because left==right==16 here there's no live RTL rendering bug today, but the checker gives false confidence: a future edit that makes left != right (a real RTL mirror bug) would ship silently, and this is the only file in the batch with this shape so the blind spot is real, not hypothetical.
finding.recommendation: Rewrite the grep to be multiline-aware (e.g. `grep -Pzo` or a small Dart/Python AST-ish scan) so it catches EdgeInsets.only(...) regardless of formatting, then replace this instance with EdgeInsetsDirectional.only(start:, end:, top:, bottom:).
acceptance_criteria: The root Makefile's AX-1 check flags a deliberately-added multi-line EdgeInsets.only(left:...) fixture.
track_management_body.dart's padding is EdgeInsetsDirectional.only(start:, end:, top:, bottom:).
`make audit` (root) still exits 0 after the fix.

finding.title: Delete or wire up the dead stage-editor mutation path (StageEditorNotifier, StageValidator, Protected/LimitExceeded exceptions)

evidence.quote: return 'Weekly stages require at least one day of week';

finding.why: A repo-wide grep for `.addStage(`, `.updateStage(`, `.deleteStage(`, `.reorderStages(` finds callers only inside stage_providers.dart itself (the notifier calling its own repository) and stage_definition_repository_impl.dart/stage_definition_repository.dart (the definitions) — StageEditorNotifier's five mutation methods have zero external callers (stageEditorProvider's only other reference, in curriculum_settings_screen.dart, is a bare ref.invalidate). That makes StageEditorNotifier.addStage/updateStage/deleteStage/reorderStages/resetToDefaults (stage_providers.dart), the repository's addStage/updateStage/deleteStage/reorderStages (stage_definition_repository_impl.dart + .../repositories/stage_definition_repository.dart), all of StageValidator, and both ProtectedStageException/StageLimitExceededException dead: ~200 lines of validated, exception-typed, individually-tested code that no screen can currently reach. It also means the EH-5 raw-English-message design smell in these exceptions (and in ArgumentError(validationError)) has zero live blast radius today, but would need fixing the moment anyone wires a stage-editor UI to this path.
finding.recommendation: Either delete the whole unreachable path (StageEditorNotifier's 5 methods, the repository's 4 corresponding methods, StageValidator, and the two exception classes) if the feature was superseded by the chazara wizard's applyWizardResult, or — if a stage-editor screen is actually planned — wire it up now and fix EH-5 (stable error codes, not raw strings) and SM-5 (state = AsyncLoading()/AsyncValue.guard around the mutation itself, not just the refetch) before shipping it.
acceptance_criteria: grep for `.addStage(`/`.updateStage(`/`.deleteStage(`/`.reorderStages(` on StageDefinitionRepository either returns a real UI caller, or the dead methods/files are removed.

If kept: StageEditorNotifier's mutation methods wrap the repository call itself in AsyncValue.guard with a preceding AsyncLoading, and the exceptions carry stable codes resolved via AppLocalizations at the presentation boundary.
Existing tests (stage_exceptions_test.dart, stage_definition_repository_impl_test.dart) still pass after whichever choice is made.
